milestones.framework: Fear AI Behavioral Evaluation Benchmark (FABE, FABE v2, and Cross-Scenario Invariance LOSO V2.1 Scientific Closure)
milestones.attribution: Evaluation design informed by controlled, replayable affective-simulation principles seen in work such as AffectSim (August 2026).
test_evidence: Major Empirical Discovery & Milestone Reclassification: On cross-scenario persona identity retrieval, Utility AI achieves 76.7% Top-1, whereas Fear AI drops from 93.3% to 18.3% (a 75 percentage-point drop). Utility AI's static polynomials preserve algebraic relationships across threat regimes; Fear AI's path-dependent dynamical state machine causes raw behavioral levels to be dominated by situational threat. Cross-scenario personality invariance is formally established as P1 research priority (Milestone Status: PARTIAL / SCIENTIFICALLY_SUCCESSFUL).

Cross-Scenario Variance Decomposition (cross_scenario_invariance_benchmark.mjs - LOSO V2.1 Scientific Closure): Evaluated 12 Scenario Families across 3 Threat Domains x Dual Cohorts (K=12 Canonical & K=60 Extended) x 10 Frozen Seeds (N=1,440 canonical, N=7,200 extended runs). Two-way ANOVA variance partitioning with seed block factor decomposes SSTotal = SSPersona + SSScenario + SSPersona x Scenario + SSSeed + SSResidual. Scenario variance accounts for 42.6% of total behavioral variance, Persona accounts for 41.1%, systematic interaction accounts for 16.3%, and seed as an ANOVA blocking factor accounts for 0.00% (within-cell residual 0.05%). Hierarchical Mixed-Model variance component estimation via Expected Mean Squares (EMS) proves that pro_social_rate has a 65.6% systematic interaction variance share (57.0% ANOVA eta^2) with 0.0% residual within-cell noise.

LOSO V2.1 Cross-Scenario Invariance & Calibration Curve: Evaluates 3 distinct normalization modes across K=12 Canonical and K=60 Extended Cohorts with crossed cluster-aware bootstraps (B=1,000) and paired fold tests (df=11 with exact Wilcoxon signed-rank W). Mode B (Sample-Limited Transductive Adaptation with leave-query-out calibration) demonstrates that just m=5 unlabelled trajectories jumps Top-1 recoverability from 31.7% to 55.7% (K=12) and 9.0% to 19.7% (K=60), saturating at m=40 (65.6% vs 66.1% Oracle). Mode C (Population Diagnostic Oracle) achieves 66.1% [Task CI: 59.1-72.4%] (K=12) and 32.3% [25.1-40.2%] (K=60 vs 1.67% chance), decisively outperforming Utility AI Oracle (35.7% at K=12, t=+6.41, p<0.0001, W=1.0; 17.4% at K=60, t=+4.44, p=0.0010, W=0.0 with 12/12 folds won). In Source-Only Inductive Model Selection (Mode A), pure mean residualization avoids mismatched SD variance scaling distortion, recovering 42.9% Top-1 (+11.2pp over SD z-score) with zero target data. Near-neighbor cross-scenario discrimination across 24 pairs (Delta=0.10) achieves 57.7% [Scen CI: 55.8-59.7%] [Pair CI: 52.7-64.3%]; trait breakdown reproduces construct validity findings: Conscientiousness (80.0%), Resilience (60.5%), and Neuroticism (55.4%) transfer robustly, while Openness (50.2%) and Agreeableness (47.6%) hover near chance. Old-4 battery isolation proves both models collapse near floor (2.9% vs 3.8% raw, 15.7% vs 18.3% oracle) in uniform shock traps without audio/peer cues; Balanced-12 families re-enable affective divergence. Distant Stalker counterexample resolved: 100% panic lock with 64.2% raw retrieval due to 30-tick gradual approach permitting pre-panic differentiation. Core behavior in packages/core/ strictly frozen.

Multivariate Clustered Factorial Inference (multivariate_trait_analysis.mjs): 5x5 factorial sweeps across 10 frozen seeds (N=250 runs, G=10 seed clusters, df=9) evaluated with Cluster-Robust Sandwich Covariance Matrix (CRVE). In N x R, additive model captures 93.22% of variance, with partial interaction contribution Delta R² = 0.97% (b1=-49.26, SE=0.13, p=3.3e-20; b2=32.47, SE=0.08, p=2.0e-20; b12=24.55, SE=0.13, p=2.2e-17). Formally classified as PREDOMINANTLY ADDITIVE MAIN EFFECTS (opposing inflow/outflow balance), not non-linear interaction.

Near-Neighbor Resolution Thresholds & Multiple Comparisons (construct_validity_sweeps.mjs): Evaluated 7 traits x 4 deltas = 28 tests (alpha_Bonferroni = 0.05/28 = 0.00179). Openness (O) is DEMONSTRATED at Delta* = 0.20 (80% [67-89%], p = 1.19e-5, survives Bonferroni). Agreeableness (A) at Delta* = 0.10 is reclassified as PROVISIONAL EVIDENCE (PENDING REPLICATION) (64% [50-76%], nominal p = 0.0325 fails Bonferroni correction; requires multi-scenario replication before freezing). N, R, E, C, L achieve Delta* = 0.05 (p < 1e-4, survives Bonferroni).

Construct Validity Monotonicity & Cross-Talk: All 7 traits demonstrate univariate Spearman monotonicity rho >= 0.85 (N: 1.0000, R: 1.0000, O: 0.9636, E: 1.0000, A: 0.9910, C: 1.0000, L: 1.0000). O, E, A, C, L pass clean isolation (|rho| <= 0.00). Under Beyond Asking standards, N and R exhibit coupled latent driver cross-talk (N -> R=-1.00, O=-0.51, A=-0.80, C=-1.00; R -> C=1.00) and are formally classified as ENTANGLED / NOT_ISOLATED.

FABE v2 Persona Repeatability (Within-Scenario, K=60 Cohort): Fear AI achieves 93.3% Top-1 [Wilson: 84.1-97.4%, Clopper-Pearson: 83.8-98.2%] (56/60) and 98.3% Top-3 [Wilson: 91.1-99.7%, Clopper-Pearson: 91.1-100.0%] (59/60) against chance (1.7% / 5.0%), with Spearman rho = 0.5498.

Paired Exact McNemar Statistical Inference: On calibrated repeatability, exact paired McNemar confirms Fear AI superiority: 19 Fear-only successes vs 3 Utility-only successes, two-sided p = 8.55e-4 (Edwards chi^2 = 10.23). On held-out unseen scenarios, exact paired McNemar confirms Utility AI superiority on cross-scenario persona identity: 3 Fear-only successes vs 38 Utility-only successes, two-sided p = 1.05e-8 (Edwards chi^2 = 28.20).

The Spearman Rank Correlation Disconnect: Behavior Tree (rho = 0.5809) and FSM (rho = 0.5999) achieve higher rank correlation than Fear AI (rho = 0.5498) while collapsing to only 2/60 (3.3%) Top-1 retrieval, proving that 1D scalar monotonicity does not measure behavioral variety without multidimensional dispersion.
Designer-Calibrated Ludological Desirability (CDS): Calibrated targets balance 46.3% habituation and 49.0% leader damping (CDS = 0.6360), preventing suicidal extinction (FSM+Memory CDS 0.2857).

Layer 2 Noise Robustness: Under +/-20% Gaussian distance error and 20% occlusion across 10 frozen seeds, Fear AI is robust under tested noise conditions with only 3.4 +/- 0.45 transitions, compared to 19.5 +/- 4.50 chatter flips for FSM and 16.4 +/- 4.25 for Utility AI.

Layer 3 Foundation: Emitted 20 randomized, double-blinded trajectory pairs to blinded_evaluation_pairs.json for human believability evaluation; baseline human annotator difficulty noted (~0.558 accuracy, kappa = 0.303).
